description: We are Nova Squad, a software-focused team tackling the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. Led by a full-stack developer skilled in Python, PHP, Node.js, and futuristic HUD design, we are building a spacecraft-style cockpit to map safe lunar landing zones using real NASA elevation data. Join us if you want to build a standout, winning project. We need frontend/3D developers (Three.js/WebGL), geospatial data analysts, and a sharp pitch strategist. Let's build the future of lunar navigation!
summary: Missions to the Moon’s south pole face extreme lighting and communication constraints, and planning them requires careful coordination between science and engineering teams. To bridge the gap between complex raw data and rapid decision-making, Nova Squad developed Vector Horizon, an intuitive web application designed for rapid lunar landing site evaluation.   Vector Horizon addresses the challenge by integrating ephemeris data from the JPL Horizons system with digital elevation models, providing interactive site selection, side-by-side scenario comparisons, and custom coordinate inputs. The application features a 3D terrain visualization and a 360-degree horizon sky-tracker that displays Sun and Earth positions relative to local topography. By calculating solar elevation angles, remaining time before sunset or Earthset, and Direct-to-Earth communication windows, it enables planners to assess power generation potential and mission feasibility instantly.   This tool is vital because mission schedules and launch dates frequently shift due to development challenges. Vector Horizon empowers engineering teams, educators, and the public to quickly evaluate alternative dates and locations, accelerating the planning process when operational constraints change.
details:
Vector Horizon is an aerospace-grade web application and flight deck HUD designed to solve the extreme lighting and communication bottlenecks at the lunar South Pole. Developed by Nova Squad,

How It Works & What It Does:

Vector Horizon integrates real-time ephemeris data from the NASA JPL Horizons API with high-resolution digital elevation models derived from LROC Quickmap. The application features an interactive 3D WebGL viewport powered by Three.js and a 360-degree horizon tracker. It calculates precise Sun and Earth elevation angles relative to local crater topography, instantly showing whether a landing site is illuminated or blocked by terrain shadows.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Lunar mission development rarely follows a fixed timeline; launch delays frequently force planners to reconsider landing dates and locations. Vector Horizon bridges the gap between raw orbital data and rapid decision-making. It enables science and engineering teams to compare Artemis candidate sites (such as Shackleton, Nobile, and Malapert Massif) or custom coordinates side-by-side. By scrubbing across a 720-hour lunar cycle, planners can instantly assess solar power flux ($W/m^2$) and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows when mission schedules shift.

Tech Stack & Software:

  • Backend & Frontend Framework: Python (NiceGUI) managing reactive state and server-client communication.
  • 3D Graphics & HUD: Three.js, HTML5, CSS3, and embedded SVG horizon charts.
  • APIs & Data Sources: NASA JPL Horizons REST API and LROC Quickmap topography.
  • Deployment: Live production hosting via Render.

Creativity & Design Factors:

We moved away from gimmicky sci-fi visuals to build a functional, data-dense engineering HUD. Key design considerations included a dual-mode toggle (Commander Mode for technical engineering telemetry and Educator Mode for public outreach), resilient offline fallback caching to ensure 100% demo uptime, and real-time temporal animation controls.
